topics.title: 2D Transforms: translate, scale, rotate, skew
topics.summary: Move, resize, rotate and skew elements without affecting layout.
topics.description:
The `transform` property changes how an element is **drawn** without changing the space it occupies in the layout. That makes it perfect (and cheap) for animation.

### Functions
| Function | Example | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `translate(x, y)` | `translate(50px, 20px)` | move; also `translateX/Y` |
| `scale(s)` / `scale(x, y)` | `scale(1.2)` | resize (1 = original) |
| `rotate(angle)` | `rotate(45deg)` | clockwise for positive |
| `skew(x, y)` | `skewX(20deg)` | slant |

### Combine functions
```css
transform: translateX(100px) scale(.5) rotate(45deg);
```
Functions are applied **right to left** in terms of coordinate effect, so order matters (rotate then translate moves along the rotated axis).

### Individual transform properties
Modern browsers also provide separate properties - easier to animate independently:

```css
translate: 100px 20px;
rotate: 45deg;
scale: .5;
```

### transform-origin
The pivot point: `transform-origin: top left;`, `center` (default), `50% 100%`, etc. Pendulums rotate around the top (used in the Newton's cradle project).

### Key facts
- Percent in `translate` refers to the element's **own size** (hence the centering trick `translate(-50%, -50%)`).
- Transforms create a stacking context and a containing block for fixed children.
- Inline elements cannot be transformed - set `display: inline-block` or block.
- Layout does not change: neighbours do not move.
keyPoints: transform draws differently but does not change layout
translate, scale, rotate, skew and their X/Y variants
pitfalls: Expecting siblings to move when an element is scaled

topics.title: 3D Transforms and Perspective
topics.summary: Use perspective, rotateX/Y and preserve-3d to build flip cards and 3D scenes.
topics.description:
CSS can transform elements in 3D space with a few extra properties.

### Core ideas
- **perspective** - distance between the viewer and the z=0 plane. Smaller value = stronger 3D effect.
- **rotateX / rotateY / rotateZ** - rotate around an axis.
- **translateZ** - move toward (+) or away (-) from the viewer.
- **transform-style: preserve-3d** - lets children live in the same 3D space instead of being flattened.
- **backface-visibility: hidden** - hide the back of an element when it is turned around.

### Two ways to set perspective
```css
.scene { perspective: 1000px; }                 /* applies to children (shared vanishing point) */
.item  { transform: perspective(600px) rotateY(30deg); } /* per element */
```
`perspective-origin` moves the vanishing point.

### Flip card recipe
```css
.card { transform-style: preserve-3d; transition: transform .8s; }
.card:hover { transform: rotateY(180deg); }
.front, .back { position: absolute; inset: 0; backface-visibility: hidden; }
.back { transform: rotateY(180deg); }
```

### Tips
- Parent needs perspective; the rotating element needs preserve-3d if it has 3D children.
- `overflow: hidden`, `opacity<1` or `filter` on an element flattens its children (breaks preserve-3d).
- Animate with transforms only - GPU friendly.
- Provide a reduced-motion alternative for big spinning effects.
keyPoints: perspective on the parent creates depth
transform-style: preserve-3d keeps children in 3D space
pitfalls: Forgetting perspective, so rotateY looks flat
Back face visible because backface-visibility is not set on both faces
Applying preserve-3d on an element whose parent flattens it

interview.q: What does the perspective property do?
interview.a: It defines how far the viewer is from the z=0 plane; applied to a parent it gives its transformed children a 3D depth effect.

interview.q: How do you build a flip card?
interview.a: Parent with perspective; inner wrapper with preserve-3d rotating on hover; front and back faces absolutely positioned with backface-visibility: hidden, back pre-rotated 180deg.

topics.title: Transitions
topics.summary: Animate property changes smoothly between two states with duration, easing and delay.
topics.description:
A **transition** animates a property from its old value to its new value when the state changes (hover, focus, class toggle by JavaScript...).

### Properties
| Property | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `transition-property` | which properties (`all`, `color`, `transform`...) |
| `transition-duration` | time, e.g. `0.3s` or `300ms` |
| `transition-timing-function` | easing: `ease`, `linear`, `ease-in`, `ease-out`, `ease-in-out`, `cubic-bezier()`, `steps()` |
| `transition-delay` | wait before starting |

### Shorthand
```css
transition: property duration timing-function delay;
transition: background-color .3s ease-in-out, transform .3s ease-out;
```

### Where to put it
Put `transition` on the **base** element (not only on :hover) so the animation works in both directions:

```css
.btn { background: #865dff; transition: all .3s linear; }
.btn:hover { background: #d80032; transform: translateY(-3px); }
```

### What can transition
Only properties with **interpolatable** values: colors, lengths, numbers, transforms, shadows, filters. `display` and `auto` sizes cannot (use `max-height`, `grid-template-rows: 0fr -> 1fr` or `transition-behavior: allow-discrete`).

### Best practice
- Animate **transform and opacity** (compositor-friendly) instead of width/height/top/left.
- Avoid `transition: all` in production; list the properties.
- Keep durations 150-400ms for UI feedback.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
keyPoints: Transition animates between two states automatically
Define it on the base state to animate both ways
Prefer transform and opacity for performance
pitfalls: Putting transition only on :hover (no animation on mouse-out)
Trying to transition display: none or height: auto

interview.q: Why is transform preferred over left/top for animation?
interview.a: Transforms can be handled by the compositor on the GPU without layout or paint, giving smoother animation.

topics.title: Keyframe Animations
topics.summary: Define multi-step animations with @keyframes and the animation-* properties.
topics.description:
Transitions need a trigger and only go from A to B. **Animations** can run automatically, loop, and have many steps.

### 1. Define keyframes
```css
@keyframes trip {
  0%   { background: #ffbb5c; transform: translate(0, 0); }
  50%  { background: #000;    transform: translate(200px, 80px); }
  100% { background: #ffbb5c; transform: translate(0, 0); }
}
/* or from { } to { } */
```

### 2. Attach it
| Property | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `animation-name` | the @keyframes name |
| `animation-duration` | length of one cycle |
| `animation-timing-function` | easing per cycle (`linear`, `ease-in-out`, `steps()`) |
| `animation-delay` | wait before start |
| `animation-iteration-count` | number or `infinite` |
| `animation-direction` | `normal`, `reverse`, `alternate`, `alternate-reverse` |
| `animation-fill-mode` | `none`, `forwards`, `backwards`, `both` |
| `animation-play-state` | `running` / `paused` |

Shorthand: `animation: trip 2.5s linear 0s infinite alternate both;`

### fill-mode explained
- `forwards`: keep the last keyframe styles after finishing.
- `backwards`: apply the first keyframe during the delay.
- `both`: both of the above.

### Notes
- No trigger needed - it can run on page load.
- You can have multiple animations: `animation: spin 2s linear infinite, pulse 1s ease-in-out infinite;`
- Use `animation-delay` with negative values to start in the middle.
- JavaScript can pause/restart by toggling classes.
- Animate `transform` and `opacity` for the best performance and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
keyPoints: @keyframes defines the steps; animation-* applies them
infinite, alternate, and fill-mode control repetition
animation-fill-mode: forwards keeps the end state
pitfalls: Animation snapping back because fill-mode is none

interview.q: Is a pseudo-class like :hover needed to start a CSS animation?
interview.a: No. Animations can start automatically on load; hover is only one way to trigger them (via changing the animation property).
It defines styles applied before the animation starts and after it ends: backwards, forwards or both.

interview.q: How do you make an animation go back and forth?

interview.a: Transitions interpolate between two states when a property changes; animations use keyframes, can run on their own, loop and have multiple steps.

interview.q: How do you create a loading spinner in CSS?
interview.a: A circle with a colored top border and an infinite linear keyframe animation rotating from 0 to 360deg.

interview.q: How do you make a typing effect?
interview.a: Use a monospace font, animate the width from 0 to the text length in ch units with steps(), hide overflow and add a blinking caret border.

interview.q: How do you respect users who prefer less motion?
interview.a: Use @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) to disable or shorten animations.
